summary: Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling, Dorje Drak, Tarje Tingpoling, and Kathok monasteries under teachers including Sera Khandro and Khenpo Aten, and founded the International Nyingma Society.

Duncan Ryūken Williams (b. 1969) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Reed College and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi (PhD 2000). He held posts at UC Irvine (~2000–2006), UC Berkeley (~2006–2011), and USC (~2011).
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. They earned a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under the doctoral supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries. He held professorships at Minzu University of China, Tibet University (~1985–1997), and served as Director at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) specialized in Indology. He studied at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, later serving as professor at Scottish Church College (~1926–1952) and Sanskrit College and University (1952).

Durga Prasad Dikshit is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri, and also studied under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.
Dwarikadas Shastri (b. 1922) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, founded Bauddha Bharati, and served as an editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indology and history scholar. He completed his education studying at Patna University (~1955–1959), Presidency University (~1959–1961), and the University of Calcutta.

Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indologist and historian who earned a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).
Dylan Esler is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at SOAS University of London and a PhD at KU Leuven (-2018), where he also served as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (b. 1964) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Nyoshul Khenpo, Tulku Urgyen, and Khenpo Rinchen, taught as professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University (1990), and founded Mangala Shri Bhuti.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (b. 1965) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under masters including the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse, later directing the Nitartha and Kamalashila institutes.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse (b. 1961) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche, and founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.

Dörte Kamarid is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher, as well as at Savitribai Phule Pune University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

E. E. Evans-Pritchard (1902–1973) studied at Exeter College, Oxford (~1921–1924) and the London School of Economics (~1924–1927). He held academic posts at LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and served at Oxford from 1946 to 1970.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry (b. 1930) is an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer and served as a Lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Kerala (attested 1973).

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetology scholar. He studied at several universities including Washington under Turrell V. Wylie, worked for the Library of Congress (1968–1985, 1994–1997), and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (1999–2010).

E. J. Rapson (1861–1937) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he worked at the British Museum before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (~1906–1936).

E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at King's College, Cambridge (~1946–1949), the University of Paris (~1949–1952), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).
E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma (1922–1994) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1951–1954) and held a post at Sri Venkateswara University (~1959–1982).
